title: Treasury International Capital (TIC) monthly release (September 2026 data) — the non-revision control edition, 4:00 p.m. ET
source: TSY: home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system/release-dates-of-tic-data, re-fetched direct by THIS event's own research session 2026-09-08 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 111,181 bytes). The 2026 table's November row reads '18' in the Monthly column under the page header 'All data releases occur at 4 p.m. Washington, D.C. time', with the Quarterly and Annual columns EMPTY for November — this is a plain monthly release. Reference month September 2026 by the page's own 1.5-month lag rule ('data on long-term securities, short-term securities, financial firms at end of month before last'). PROMOTED from estimate 2026-09-08 on the mts-october-2026-11-12 bar of one named Treasury primary + independent mechanical corroboration, the no-self-confirm limit cleared because this is the event's own session re-fetching rather than the tic-monthly-2026-10-16 sweep that discovered it. The corroboration, recomputed here from scratch: the page's published '11th business day plus 0 to 3 days' rule, with federal holidays excluded (Veterans Day 11-11, Thanksgiving 11-26), puts November 2026's 11th business day on 11-17, so the rule permits 11-17 through 11-20 and the published date sits inside at offset +1 — weaker than October's exact +0, but ROBUST TO THE CONVENTION: under the weekday-only reading (11th weekday = 11-16, window 11-16 to 11-19) 11-18 is still in-window, which is not true of every date on this schedule. The same holiday-aware convention reproduces 22 of the 24 published 2026-27 dates and hits 9 exactly; the two misses (2026-01-15, 2026-07-14) both fall EARLIER than the rule's floor, so a date inside the window is never one of the failure modes. TSY: is extended from auction schedule to release schedule on the precedent mts-august-2026-09-11, mts-october-2026-11-12, tic-monthly-2026-09-16 and tic-monthly-2026-10-16 already recorded. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: Canonical file written by this id's own initial research (2026-09-08) after reading the one proposal that created it, `from-tic-monthly-2026-10-16`, now shadowed. What this edition is FOR, in one line: it is the NON-REVISION CONTROL against its October sibling's annual-revision edition, and the control turned out to carry the stronger result. October's cut (revision months mean |d10Y| 4.00bp vs 2.55bp for the rest, t=+2.13, p=0.033) was read as 'revision months are not unusually quiet'; testing the OTHER bucket directly — the bucket this event sits in — makes the finding sharp: non-revision TIC next-sessions run mean |d10Y| 2.55bp (n=20) against 3.94bp for every session in the same 2024-03..2026-09 window (t=-3.67, p=0.0002) and 3.78bp for a day-of-month-matched mid-month control (t=-2.74, p=0.0062), while revision months are indistinguishable from both (p=0.93, p=0.73). A local-neighbourhood scan then names the mechanism honestly: the TIC next-session is the LOCAL MINIMUM of its own week (2.55bp against 4.45bp the session before and 3.30bp after), because TIC is scheduled the day AFTER the mid-month CPI/PPI/retail-sales cluster. The quiet is a calendar position, not a TIC effect, and it is not a trade. THE TAPE TEST THIS EVENT CANNOT RUN: 2026-11-18 carries FOMC minutes at 14:00 and a 20-Year new-issue auction at 13:00, and the scored next session 11-19 carries a 10-Year TIPS auction — so of this calendar's three TIC prints, exactly one (10-16) is testable and it is not this one. Impact LOW and symbols empty for the standing reasons (16:00 ET is after the equity cash close, the data is six weeks stale, no house playbook is macro-keyed). Existence risk is nil here: PL 119-103 funds agencies through 2026-12-11, three weeks past this date, so the lapse branch that cancelled the October 2025 release reaches tic-monthly-2026-12-15 and not this one. Nothing here licenses an entry.
